One conversation.
One captured case.

A tester flags one answer and explains why. The complete shopping journey, its tool evidence, and what the browser actually showed become one reviewable case.

Agent Studio history existsCapture and admin views proposedDelivery trace still missing
The test of success is binary.

After a multi-turn JTV conversation, a visitor selects Capture on one message, enters a required comment, and receives a case ID. An admin opens that ID and sees every turn with validated links to Agent Studio records and the focused feedback. A failed reply is recorded as failed, even if Agent Studio stored the answer.

01 / The journey

Where one case comes from

The sketch is the meeting story. The editable architecture below names the exact system boundaries and ownership.

Executive sketch. Current Agent Studio capabilities are stages 1 and 2; JTV’s browser display exists today but its outcome trace is proposed. Capture, case assembly and admin review are proposed for the pilot.

1. AskAgent Studio conversation stores the question.
2. ActClient tools record state, retrieval and results.
3. ShowJTV browser displays an answer, cards or an error.
4. FlagVisitor selects a message and must add a comment.
5. AssembleServer validates native IDs and stores the case.
6. ReviewAdmin sees the full journey and may export it.

04 / System architecture

Keep the native log. Add the missing handoffs.

Agent Studio remains the authority for messages and tools. JTV stores message-focused comments, browser outcomes and immutable evidence snapshots in a managed database.

SOURCE 1 · EXISTING

Agent Studio

Conversation ID, messages, structured tool calls and results, answer text and feedback.

SOURCE 2 · NEW

JTV turn trace

Actual proxy stream ending, tool boundary, browser finish, card commit and notice outcome.

JOIN · NEW

Capture service

Validate native IDs, focus one message, require a comment and assemble the whole journey.

REVIEW · NEW

Private case store

Managed PostgreSQL plus locked admin view, daily queue and controlled export.

journeyId → conversationId(s) → turnId → messageId → toolCallId(s) + streamLegId(s) → browser outcome → captureId

Storage choice: Managed PostgreSQL is the selected pilot path. A dedicated private Algolia index could hold small reference records, but one measured 43-message JTV transcript is 533,487 bytes, above Algolia’s 10 KB free or 100 KB paid per-record limit. Agent Studio owns native history; the private case store holds a dated evidence snapshot and any failed question that never reached Agent Studio.

05 / API truth

Most agent-side evidence is already there

The meeting proposal should credit the native Agent Studio capabilities. The missing product layer is the joined conversation review and the last-mile browser outcome.

Needed for the caseAvailable todayAdditional work
Whole conversationAgent Studio Conversation GET/export has ordered messages, IDs and timestamps.JTV journey lineage when history appears in multiple native conversation records.
Question before a failed sendIt may be absent from Agent Studio if the request failed before native persistence.Retain submitted text briefly in the private case store and label it JTV-app-sourced if native history never appears.
Words to structureState tool inputs and accepted/rejected results show observable conversion.Display the before/after brief; do not claim private model thoughts.
Queries and evidenceRetrieve tool inputs and results include requested query, effective filters and evidence.Capture exact lower-level search requests/retries and card commit outcome.
Answer and thumbsAssistant text and feedback API exist. Live agent feedback is enabled.JTV custom renderer needs thumbs controls and response handling.
Tester’s commentFeedback API supports one vote per assistant message, optional notes.Required message-focused comment and no-assistant failure capture need JTV case storage.
Seen on screenNot proved by Agent Studio’s stored answer or staged product result.Record stream end, browser finish/error, rendered cards and notice.

Evidence already measured

A JTV Conversation GET returned 43 messages. One assistant message contained four tool calls and their results, followed by generated text. Another conversation record repeated 23 message IDs from an earlier record.

What we cannot honestly claim

The API does not expose private model chain of thought. A native saved answer does not prove the shopper received it. The historic 15-second notice needs browser/proxy handoff events to identify its exact cause.

06 / GLM execution contract

One big goal. Small loops that must pass.

GLM builds one bounded slice, compares it to “good,” saves the test receipt, and stops on the first failure. A green unit test never substitutes for the connected JTV screen.

Loop 1

Identity and source contract

One journey maps to native conversations and turns. Inherited messages dedupe by ID. A failed turn without an assistant ID remains addressable.

Loop 2

Turn handoff evidence

Proxy, tool and browser outcomes join under one turn. Injected failures identify the right boundary without changing SSE bytes.

Loop 3

Durable case backend

Required comment, focused message, validated native references and full-conversation snapshot create one idempotent capture ID.

Loop 4

Visitor capture and thumbs

Accessible message-level dialog blocks blank comments. Completed answers have native thumbs. Failed notices still have Capture.

Loop 5

Daily review and export

Authorized admins see captured and automatic failures, inspect full chronology and export a controlled evidence package.

Loop 6

Connected release

Real JTV journeys, failure injection, mobile checks, CI, exact version readback and canonical production smoke all pass before “working” is claimed.

Stop rule: If a loop cannot produce its stated browser/API receipt, GLM fixes that loop before starting the next. No customer catalogue-index change, no second agent, no second Vercel project, and no production claim from a mock screen or saved Agent Studio text alone.
07 / Agent Studio product opportunity

Make conversation review native

JTV can prove the use case. An out-of-the-box Agent Studio feature would remove the app-specific assembly work for every future customer.

Native Capture API

Anchor required annotations to a message or a failed user turn, return a case ID, preserve conversation lineage, and support validated source links without forcing a thumbs vote.

Delivery event contract

Accept signed browser outcomes for stream finish, rendered response, cards and notices. Preserve the distinction between agent completion and shopper-visible delivery.

Conversation review workspace

Show a whole conversation, each turn, tool spans, evidence and focused feedback in one chronology. Flag automatic failures and deduplicate inherited message history.

Secure sharing

Admin roles, retention, redaction, export and audit logs. SDK controls should work for both prebuilt Chat and custom useChat renderers.

08 / Sources and limits

What this proposal rests on

  • Algolia Conversations guide, complete conversation retrieval and retention.
  • Algolia per-turn context guide, stored user-turn context and its limits.
  • Algolia feedback guide, one vote per assistant message, optional tags and notes.
  • Algolia record-size guidance, used to evaluate the private-index alternative.
  • Read-only JTV Agent Studio GET, October 16, 2026: 43-message conversation, 51 tool call/result pairs, compact JSON 533,487 bytes. No shopper transcript is embedded in this page.
  • JTV October 15 incident ledger: agent answer saved while browser showed “That message did not go through.” Exact stream-ending component remains unproven.
